question.problem:
Given the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $u?$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
We compute the dot product between $u$ and each of the listed vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =5\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 0+4\cdot 2 \\  & =5+6+0+8 \\  & =19.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & ={u}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {w}_{4} \\  & =5\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 2 \\  & =-5-4+1+8 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot x & ={u}_{1}\cdot {x}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {x}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {x}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {x}_{4} \\  & =5\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 2+4\cdot (-2) \\  & =0+2-2-8 \\  & =-8.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the correct option is $w$ only.
